root_cause.text: The BPF JIT buffer allocation used 4-byte alignment instead of 8-byte alignment, which allowed the base address to be misaligned relative to the 8-byte alignment required for atomic access to the `u64 target` field in `struct bpf_plt`, causing potential torn reads when updated concurrently via `WRITE_ONCE`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch increases the alignment parameter in `bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc()` from `sizeof(u32)` (4 bytes) to `sizeof(u64)` (8 bytes). The commit message explains that "the base address of the JIT buffer can be 4-byte aligned ... the relative padding logic in build_plt() fails to ensure that target lands on an 8-byte boundary" and that "64-bit loads/stores are only guaranteed to be single-copy atomic if they are 64-bit aligned." This directly identifies the misalignment as the root cause of the vulnerability.

intent_record.how: The allocated memory region will now be aligned to 8 bytes instead of 4 bytes, which may be required for proper operation on 64-bit architectures, especially for instruction or data access.

candidates.rationale: This line specifies 4-byte alignment (sizeof(u32)) in bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc, which should have been 8-byte alignment (sizeof(u64)). The insufficient alignment causes the base address of the BPF JIT buffer to be misaligned for atomic 8-byte access to the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt, leading to potential torn reads when updated via WRITE_ONCE.
